reasons.A: Long semicolon-linked sentences with balanced clauses, a confiding first person ('I cannot help thinking') and plain period diction, all at the passage's own density without overdoing it.
reasons.C: Right period register and semicolon rhythm, but it stacks hedges ('perhaps', 'I am inclined myself to think', 'so to speak'), adds an exclamation and a lamp metaphor, so it reads as a thickened imitation.
reasons.B: Shorter, evenly paced modern sentences, few semicolons and a neutral contemporary register ('under pressure', 'life story'); it lacks the passage's Edwardian cadence and confessional warmth.
